**Tier G** — governance — identity, capability, delegation, audit · owned by `platform` · `public.organizations`

**One row is** One tenant. Every project, every dataset and every simulation result in the product belongs to exactly one of these rows, and the boundary between two of them is the boundary the whole access layer is built to hold.

Created by `20260709000002_super_admin_phase1.sql`, which seeded one row per DISTINCT `approved_users.organization` string. That seeding is why the uuid plane and the text plane started out agreeing, and why nothing has kept them agreeing since: the seed ran once, `set_project_defaults()` never stamped the uuid (D27), and `admin_update_organization` renames without propagating. WP 2.1 fixed the trigger, backfilled what it could match unambiguously, and routed every live comparison through one predicate. It deliberately did NOT re-seed this table from distinct strings: after a rename, a user carrying the new name slugifies to a slug no row holds, and seeding would split one organization into two.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | `super_admin` |
| Minimum project role | `viewer` |
| Tier transitions audited | yes |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 2 — all carry a predicate |

`write: super_admin` is enforced, not aspirational: every mutation goes through `admin_create_organization` / `admin_update_organization` / `admin_set_org_status` / `admin_set_org_access_period` / `admin_set_org_limits` / `admin_delete_organization`, each of which opens with `_assert_super_admin` and closes with `log_admin_action`. The last is §4 D208: a PERMANENT delete that takes the organization's projects and accounts with it, and is a different verb from suspension — since §4 D210 only the accounts that belong to NO other organization; an account that also belongs elsewhere loses this membership and keeps the rest. This is one of the few tables where `audited: true` is literally true today — WP 2.3 is what makes the claim general. Read is open to any member of the org via the self-bridge policy below, which WP 2.1 rewrote: it matched the caller's TEXT org against `name` or `slug`, so renaming an organization revoked its own members' read on the row that had just been renamed. It now bridges on `id` first.

<details><summary>2 RLS policies</summary>

| Policy | Command | Roles | Added by |
|---|---|---|---|
| orgs: super admin full | ALL | all | `20260709000002_super_admin_phase1.sql` |
| orgs: members read own | SELECT | all | `20260918000001_org_row_uuid_only.sql` |

</details>

> D13's join key. `admin_update_organization` updates this column and nothing else: no trigger, no cascade, and no second UPDATE reaching `approved_users.organization` or `projects.organization`. So a rename leaves those two text copies holding the OLD string, and the next user approved into the organization carries the NEW one — at which point a text comparison between them can never match again. WP 2.1 routes every such comparison through `org_is_current_user_org(uuid, text)`.

> SUSPENSION IS NOT ENFORCED IN THE DATA LAYER. No policy and no RPC consults this column before granting access — a suspended organization's members read and write exactly as before. It is a label the admin pages render. Recorded here rather than left to be discovered, per §5 T1; the enforcement belongs with WP 2.2's resolver, which is where a capability decision is made once instead of inevery policy.
